newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds saw earlier gains eroded as U.S. Treasuries opened weaker, but they still showed modest gains at the close.
The January 2006 bond closed 0.19 higher at 102.91/99 for a bid yield of 5.57 percent, a steady 14 basis points below the yield on the April 2006 German bund.
Prices of guilder bonds had shown much stronger gains earlier in the day on favourably received inflation data from the U.S. and, to a lesser extent, Germany and the Netherlands.
But prices retreated as U.S. Treasuries were hit by corporate supply and the dollar slipping from its recent highs.
The five to 10 year yield spread in guilder bonds was steady with an unchanged gap of 108 basis points between the January 2006 and the September 2001 issue.

But the yield gap between the short end of the curve and the middle steepend again after a recent flattening, with the 6.25 percent July 1998 bond yielding 122 basis points below the September 2001, compared with 119 basis points on Tuesday.

Dealers said the announcement of a Dutch government bond sale on Friday morning and U.S. industrial output and capacity utilisation data later that day were the key market events for the rest of this week.
Most dealers expect a re-opening of the 5.75 percent September 2002 bond, of which there is currently some 7.5 billion guilders outstanding.
The government, which has sharply reduced borrowing needs this year, has said it favours a minimum issue size of 10 billion guilders.
Some dealers believe a new 10-year benchmark issue with a January 2007 maturity is also possible.
